hook_text: Five sweets. You eat one. The packet now remembers — and that memory is worth marks in Paper One.
clip_script: A packet of five sweets: three red, two blue. You take one, eat it, take another. Easy? Here's what most people miss: the packet REMEMBERS. First draw — three out of five for red. But the second draw never faces five sweets. It faces four survivors — and WHICH four depends on what you ate. Ate a red? Two red, two blue left — fifty-fifty. Ate a blue? Three red, one blue — the odds just shifted. That's what 'without replacement' really means: every branch of the story carries new arithmetic. The tree diagram is just the story drawn with its worlds attached. Then two moves finish everything. AND multiplies along a path: red then red is three fifths times two quarters — three tenths. OR adds across paths: one of each colour can happen two ways, six twentieths plus six twentieths — three fifths. And here's the pro move nobody uses: add ALL your path products at the end. They must total exactly one — every future accounted for. Twenty twentieths. If yours don't hit one, the tree just told you which branch is broken. Free receipt, every question.
visual_style: A crinkly sweet packet spills into an animated branching tree; each branch grows a tiny inventory tag of remaining sweets, path probabilities light up and multiply, and a till-slip receipt prints '20/20 = 1' at the end.
pacing: Quick setup, beat on 'the packet REMEMBERS', rhythmic multiply-along add-across chant, confident receipt reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make trees, tables and triple Venns do the thinking for you.
